column2: A galley appliance remains energized during a fire. Which extinguisher classification covers that hazard?
column7: Class C covers fires in energized electrical equipment. The extinguishing medium must avoid conducting electricity.

column2: How are the spot switches connected when any one closed switch must light the fire warning?
column7: A parallel branch lets a single thermal switch complete the warning circuit. A series circuit would require all the switches to close.

column2: A thermocouple fire detector sees both junctions warm equally. Why does its relay stay open?
column7: Both junctions are at the same temperature. A rapid local increase at the exposed junction creates the voltage that operates the warning circuit.

column2: What makes a continuous-loop detector suitable for monitoring a long nacelle compartment?
column7: The sensing element follows the protected area and responds to heat along its length. A spot detector monitors conditions at its own location.

column2: An optical sensor looks into a fire zone. Which signal indicates a hydrocarbon flame?
column3: Radiation in a selected wavelength band
column4: Increased resistance in a sensing wire
column5: Pressure rise in a sealed gas tube
column7: An optical detector responds to characteristic infrared or ultraviolet emissions. Its spectral response distinguishes this method from measuring temperature electrically or pneumatically.

column2: Which change operates the electrical contact on an extinguisher bottle's combination gauge switch?
column7: The gauge provides a local reading. The switch changes state when the container loses pressure, allowing a remote indication.

column2: A bottle gauge reads lower after a cold soak. Which reference establishes the acceptable range?
column7: Container pressure varies with temperature. The chart gives the allowed pressure range for the temperature at which the reading is taken.

column2: Which extinguisher bottle component protects the container if external heating produces excessive internal pressure?
column7: The diaphragm relieves excessive pressure caused by heat. A low-pressure switch reports a pressure loss but does not provide overpressure protection.

column2: What is the maximum time from cargo fire ignition to flight crew visual indication under Part 25?
column7: The certification requirement measures one minute from the start of a cargo or baggage compartment fire to its visual indication to the flight crew.

column2: What initiates required built-in suppression in a transport airplane lavatory paper disposal receptacle?
column7: The built-in extinguisher discharges automatically into the affected receptacle when a fire occurs there. Lavatory smoke detection provides a separate warning.

column2: A cabin carbon monoxide alert appears when exhaust-shroud heat is selected. Which defect fits?
column7: Exhaust can enter the cabin heating airflow through a damaged exhaust system. Incomplete combustion produces carbon monoxide, which has no odor of its own.

column2: On a Boeing 777 with both engine detector loops serviceable, what triggers an engine fire warning?
column7: Normal operation requires agreement between the two engine fire detection channels. The system handles faults and overheat indications separately.

column2: On an articulated rotor, which hinge accommodates a blade moving forward in its plane of rotation?
column7: The drag hinge allows an individual blade to lead or lag in the rotor plane. Flapping changes the blade's position above or below that plane.

column2: On a two-blade semirigid rotor, what happens to the opposite blade when one blade flaps up?
column7: The semirigid hub teeters as one unit. As one blade rises relative to the hub, the opposite blade moves down.

column2: A blade twists about its spanwise axis as the pitch link moves. Which motion is occurring?
column7: Feathering changes blade pitch about its lengthwise axis. Flapping and lead-lag move the blade in different planes around the hub.

column2: Which assembly transfers motion from nonrotating helicopter flight controls to rotating main rotor pitch links?
column7: The stationary part of the swashplate receives pilot inputs. The rotating part carries those inputs to the blade pitch links.

column2: What pitch change should a collective input produce with the cyclic held steady?
column5: Change on the advancing side alone
column7: The collective changes every blade's pitch by the same amount at the same time. Cyclic pitch varies with a blade's position around the disk.

column2: A helicopter pilot moves the cyclic forward from a stable hover. Which part tilts forward?
column7: Cyclic pitch varies through the revolution and changes blade flapping. The resulting tip-path plane tilts in the direction of the control input.

column2: Which component lets the rotor transmission overrun the engine as engine speed falls after power loss?
column7: The one-way drive releases when the rotor side turns faster than the engine side. The rotor can continue turning without driving the slowing engine.

column2: A helicopter transmission has a 9:1 reduction and a 3,150 rpm input. What is rotor speed?
column7: The reduction means the input turns nine times for each output revolution. Dividing 3,150 by nine gives 350 rpm at the rotor.

column2: How do pedal inputs change yaw in a conventional single-main-rotor helicopter with a tail rotor?
column7: Changing tail rotor blade pitch changes sideways thrust. This changes the moment about the helicopter's vertical axis.

column2: Two numbered targets appear at different heights under a synchronized strobe. Which condition does this reveal?
column7: A tracking strobe makes each tip target appear stationary. The relative target heights show whether the blades follow the same rotational path.

column2: A two-blade rotor produces one vertical shake per revolution. Which condition best explains that frequency?
column7: A once-per-revolution vertical vibration can result when the blades develop different lift at the same point in rotation. Higher-speed drive components usually excite different frequencies.

column2: Which R66 landing gear component takes a permanent set to absorb a hard landing impact?
column7: The R66 center crosstube is designed to yield under a hard landing load. The manufacturer also specifies a separate hard landing inspection.

column2: In a transport airplane's plumbed potable system, which lavatory fixture normally shares the galley water supply?
column7: The potable tank supplies the galley and lavatory faucet through distribution piping. The waste tank and its drain belong to a separate system.

column2: Which service-panel connection carries surplus water outside once a potable tank reaches its fill level?
column7: The overflow line provides a separate path from the tank to the service panel. The tank drain is used to empty the system deliberately.

column2: What is the purpose of the disk near the nozzle on an aircraft potable-water service hose?
column3: Keep the nozzle off the ground
column5: Limit insertion depth at the panel
column6: Calibrate flow into the fill line
column7: The disk keeps the open end clear of contaminated ground if the hose is dropped. A cover protects the nozzle while it is stored.

column2: On a multi-tap airliner, which pair of outlets supplies the two routine coliform samples?
column7: The aircraft drinking water rule requires one routine sample from the galley and one from the lavatory when both are present. Each represents water delivered to users.

column2: A carrier disinfects and flushes each aircraft water system every four months. How often is routine coliform sampling due at minimum?
column7: The aircraft drinking water rule pairs a four-month disinfection and flushing interval with sampling at least twice a year. The maximum interval between routine sampling rounds is six months.

column2: A pressure reversal drives contaminated water toward the supply. Which component should have blocked that flow?
column7: A backflow prevention device protects the potable supply against reverse flow. Its condition is among the items checked during the aircraft water-system self-inspection.

column2: Where does the A330-700L send used washbasin water during normal operation?
column7: Airbus routes galley sink and lavatory washbasin drainage overboard on this model. The toilet sends its contents to the waste tank.

column2: Which A330-700L waste service connection accepts the hose that carries tank contents to the servicing vehicle?
column7: The waste service installation has a four-inch drain valve and a separate one-inch connection for flushing and filling. The two connections serve different directions of flow.

column2: Which source supplies the bowl rinse on an aircraft equipped with the Diehl InnoLite toilet?
column7: The unit uses clean water from the aircraft's potable supply for rinsing. A separate pressure difference moves waste into the collection tubing.

column2: Once a vacuum toilet's outlet opens, what carries waste from the bowl into its collection line?
column4: Higher pressure in the waste tank
column7: The pressure difference draws waste from the higher-pressure bowl toward the lower-pressure collection line. Rinse water serves a separate function.

column2: What must the location and design of a Part 25 overboard fluid drain prevent?
column7: The design must prevent hazardous ice from forming on the aircraft when fluids that can freeze drain overboard. The requirement covers both ground and flight operation.

column2: An A220 is being serviced at the potable water drains. Which hazard is associated with the mast itself?
column4: Pressure from a sealed waste tank
column7: The A220 potable water draining procedure warns that the drain mast can become hot enough to injure a person who touches it.
